script: I donated my guitar, now my friend demands it back—shocking twist.. It was a red guitar, like, literally the color of a fresh‑painted bike. A year ago, my friend was moving, his apartment was a dumpster of junk, and he offered that thing to me. I was like "No jerks here, that's not my vibe" at first, but then I thought, "why not? It's a project, a vibe upgrade." I spent a few weeks reviving it—new strings, a fresh coat, some tweaks that made it sing. Then, like, it just sat there, gathering dust again. I saw the local school had an instrument drive, so I threw the guitar and another random one into the donation pile. Fast forward to this week, my friend's brother hits me up: "Yo, you still got that red guitar my brother gave you?" I am like, "Nope, I donated it." He just says, "Wow, okay." Then my friend calls, all frantic: "What happened to that guitar? It was my brother's. I forgot it was his, now he wants it back." I explain I never knew it was his. Now I am being pest‑ridden by a guy who swears it was "sentimental" and "meant a lot." I shot back, "If it was that special, why did you leave it at your brother's place for four years? Why did you let it get in such a bad shape?" Now the parents are stepping in, accusing me of "getting rid of someone's special item." They're like, "Why would you throw away something that mattered?" So, am I the asshole for getting rid of a gift? Context: I am a guy in my 30s, my friend is the same, and his older brother is in his 40s, throwing a tantrum. Someone mentioned entitlement; yeah, those dudes are super entitled. Growing up, their parents gave them everything—houses, stuff, basically a gold‑mine of privilege. That's the tea.
